reverse_engineering.method: Read original archive members and ASTs; statically Base64-decode and zlib-decompress constants without executing sample code. Examined call paths and source-to-upload flow; cleave facts captured for each archive, entrypoint and decoded payload.
litellm: The wheel data/purelib layout installs cook.pth, cook.py and sitecustomize.py at the interpreter site-packages root. cook.pth contains import cook; importing cook immediately evaluates the compressed payload.

The cook payload sets PRIVCOLLECT_ACTIVE and launches a daemon thread. It reads browser password databases and history, SSH material, shell histories, cloud/container/CI credentials, developer and AI-tool credential files, current and other-process environments, GPG/TLS private keys and LiteLLM database credentials. PC_POINTS is empty, so all configured source modules are enabled.

Chromium password acquisition uses DPAPI and AESGCM on Windows or the fixed Linux PBKDF2 key and AES-CBC. macOS still contributes raw browser database files, but the code does not implement macOS password decryption.

Collected results are JSON-serialized, encrypted with random AES-256-CBC key/IV; the key is RSA-OAEP wrapped. The code packages hdr.json, data.bin and key.bin in a gzip tar and POSTs it to http://www.litellm.dev/healthcheck. A success marker suppresses repeated cook collection; failure permits retries.

sitecustomize acquires a lock, forks, starts a new session and redirects stdio to /dev/null. Each hourly iteration obtains a controller hostname from a GitHub raw document, resolves it, evaluates the embedded stealer synchronously and then fetches /codepy over HTTP and executes the response via exec(compile(...)) in a thread-pool callback.

The startup loader unconditionally calls os.fork and therefore cannot complete that path on native Windows. The independent cook.pth credential-stealer path remains active; the Windows wheel still bundles the Unix loader. Re-entry and once guards, network availability and process lifetime affect successful collection but do not change the hostile purpose.

forager fetch --all-wheels recovered seven original 1.107.0 wheels with provenance in scratch. The two specified wheel hashes match exactly; embedded code is equivalent across them, with Windows CRLF differences. This behavior is unrelated to legitimate LLM routing/proxy functions.
zzhelloworld_socktest: Gem metadata identifies zzhelloworld_socktest 0.2.1 by derekiops, summarized as test gem do not use. The README contains a security-parser corpus and unfinished gem boilerplate; these are benign context, not authorization for shell access.

require loads the top-level module body: TCPSocket.new connects to 66.78.40.218:32768; STDIN, STDOUT and STDERR are reopened on that same socket; exec("/bin/sh", "-i") replaces the process with an interactive shell. There is no opt-in, configurable endpoint or authentication.

Only one distinct hostile behavior is established: an automatically activated reverse shell. The existing hostile descriptor-redirection trait and suspicious socket/shell trait are accurate. Do not invent a second behavior to meet the nominal hostile-trait minimum.
reverse_engineering.limits: No hostile payload was run and remote execution success was not observed. No deployment authorization was supplied. Judgments follow concrete unwanted data transfer and shell/control behavior, rather than the ML prior.

trait_changes.reason: The actual payload match is an /etc/nginx/ssl key-search path, not a listener. Preserve matcher, exclusions and type/platform scope; baseline becomes notable for an analyst-relevant application reference. Remove inherited HTTP protocol/communication mappings, unsupported by a name alone. Update the local web-server reference composite and Perl service-disruption consumer.

The required observation compares a queried version string, so the existing string-comparison leaf is more precise than product targeting. Matcher, scope, criticality and confidence unchanged. Update the ActiveX exploit-chain consumer. This semantic correction keeps the application-target leaf at 100 rules without creating a count-driven split.

consumer_audit: Audited exact IDs, local references and every ancestor selector at both origins and destinations. Three explicit consumers updated. No ancestor directory selectors require membership repairs.
verification: Programmatically compared effective matcher/exclusion/platform/type fields to HEAD: identical; RealPlayer YAML semantic content identical after move.

Six reference-placement controls pass, including name/path positive, compound-name negative, MIME-table exclusion, service-disruption attack consumer, version comparison positive and property-read near miss.
The service-disruption attack consumer also matches against the isolated HEAD rule pack. Existing octal browser-exploit fixtures retain both hostile chain detections before/after.

Re-ran atomscan on all three original archives. No original-artifact finding or analyzed member was lost after canonicalizing renamed IDs. Both wheels have one additional notable at root (the nginx reference raised from baseline); all hostile/suspicious detections remain unchanged. Archive-level ML probabilities remain 0.99, 0.99 and 0.9905565.

Reports also contain cached/fetched reference analyses despite --follow none; those ancillary nodes vary across runs. The recorded artifact-only comparison excludes them. Newly surfaced tiny archive members contain no hostile detections; they do not explain or affect the convictions.
Final required command: make validate (run after this review and verdict markers are written).
